entries.grounds: `required` (adapters.py:197) goes to three places in code: review_ocr.coverage(output, ..., required=required, ...) (adapters.py:252-253), whose first statement is `required = sorted(set(required))` (review_ocr.py:80) - so `missing[:10]`, the excluded/absent lists and every reason (review_ocr.py:118-127) are derived from a copy sorted there and do not depend on the caller's order; review_ocr.findings(output, required) (adapters.py:261) which builds `set(required)` (review_ocr.py:144, membership for `in_scope`); and the session record (`"required": required`, adapters.py:250 -> self.sessions -> RUN.json `sessions`, run.py:488-497, only `text` stripped; EVIDENCE.json hashes RUN.json by its canonical JSON, run.py:278-301). The mutant yields git's own row order instead of the order of the decoded text. They coincide for every valid-UTF-8, CR-free path (tree order = full-path byte order = code-point order; measured). They differ where git's bytes and the decoded text disagree: an invalid UTF-8 byte (U+FFFD) and, new in this entry, a CR (the shared git helper's text mode turns it into LF). Then one list in RUN.json is ordered differently. Hence AUDITED, not EQUIVALENT. No code reads that order. The tests that read `s['required']` all compare to sorted(valid CR-free names) (a docstring even says 'required, sorted': test_v21_defects_ocr.py test_ordinary_rows_are_read_as_before), which git's own order satisfies, so they pass under the mutant.

entries.grounds: Re-derived at the snapshot (story_runner.py, proof.py, routing.py, outcome.py, format3.py, merge.py are byte-identical to c4c1720, i.e. to the proof's own base). Value flow: story_runner.py:247-248 builds `preserved` (ObligationRole is read at no other line of the module but :139 `o.role.value` from plan.obligations); :250 `spec_id, role = obligations.get(cid) or preserved[cid]` (the plan's own role wins whenever the cid is one of the story's obligations); :251-253 hands `role` to prove() with the literal point MeasurementPoint.CANDIDATE. In prove() (proof.py:80-111) `role` is read once, at :107 `route(bound, spec, point, role)`; prove() refuses PARENT first (:86-87); the Proof (:28-37), the probe/evaluated payloads (plain(record)), the proof/verified payload (format3.verified_payload :233-246) and the gate row (`proof:{cid}`, :255-256) carry no role, and the Party range name is built from `under = criterion/point` (:88, :69). In route/row_for (routing.py:96-130) role has three readers: the isinstance guard (:114-115; all three labels are ObligationRole members), the table lookup (:125-126) and the fail-closed text (:102-103). Every role-keyed row of _EXECUTED is at PARENT (:70, :73, :76); the CANDIDATE rows (:81-86) are keyed role None, so .get((C, sat, reason, label)) misses and the `or` falls to (C, sat, reason, None): the same Route for any label. The fail-closed text is reachable only when row_for returns None; at CANDIDATE it cannot, by totality: Executed.__post_init__ (outcome.py:43-50) allows a reason only on INDETERMINATE and only an IndeterminateReason, which has exactly PRECONDITION_ABSENT and NON_CONTROLLER_SIGNAL (:28-33); contract_satisfaction (:71-79) yields SATISFIED/UNSATISFIED (no reason) or INDETERMINATE; the table has (C,S,None), (C,U,None), (C,I,PA), (C,I,NCS); UNRUNNABLE/INVALID_SPEC return at routing.py:120-123 before the lookup. The only place INTRODUCE differs from PRESERVE in the table is the PARENT PRECONDITION_ABSENT row (:70 READY vs :73 PRECONDITION_BROKEN); PARENT is refused by prove() before any role is read, so that row is unreachable from this call site (story_admission.py:80, the PARENT caller, passes the plan's obligation.role).
